notesDetails.title: Upfront Source-Code Probing Prevented Two Major Architecture Traps (S0)
bullets: 20.0 Active Minutes of Probing Before S1 (Lines 1–38): The agent spent 37 LLM calls and 51.9k output tokens running empirical probes in /tmp and inspecting local Erlang/OTP 28 source files before touching project code.

1. Uncovering an Erlang :httpc Streaming Blind Spot (Lines 25–37): After writing /tmp/probe_httpc.exs, the agent grepped ~/.nix-profile/lib/erlang/lib/inets-9.6.2.3/src/http_client/httpc_handler.erl and found -define(IS_STREAMED(Code), ((Code =:= 200) orelse (Code =:= 206))) (line 34). It proved that :httpc with stream: :self never delivers the HTTP status code on 200/206 responses ({RequestId, :stream_end, Headers}) and buffers the full body in memory for all other status codes. That led it to build a zero-dependency HTTP/1.1 client over :gen_tcp and :ssl (lib/capy_bench/http/conn.ex and lib/capy_bench/http.ex) with exact monotonic deadlines.

2. Solving BEAM SIGINT & Escript Handling Upfront (Lines 7–23): It verified that OTP 28 rejects :os.set_signal(:sigint, :handle), proved in /tmp that +Bi -noinput disables the BEAM break handler cleanly, and validated replacing :erl_signal_server's default handler via :gen_event.delete_handler/3 + :gen_event.add_handler/3 so a POSIX ./cb wrapper could forward SIGINT as SIGTERM directly to the runner PID.

notesDetails.title: Freemium Concurrency Limiter Triggered on Sub-85ms Turnarounds (10 Errors)
bullets: 10 Failed Requests on zai-start-plan (Lines 24, 59, 73, 98, 115, 132, 160, 163, 202, 221): All 10 aborted turns failed with TerminalStreamChunkError: model concurrency limit exceeded on attempt: 1 despite zero parallel LLM calls.

Sub-85ms Turnaround Race: In 8 of the 10 errors (lines 59, 73, 98, 132, 160, 163, 202, 221), the preceding tool call was a fast local operation (Edit, Read, or grep) that completed in 21ms to 81ms (0.021s–0.081s). ZCode immediately opened the next SSE stream before the gateway finished releasing the prior stream's concurrency slot.

No Automatic Backoff Retry: Because ZCode treated TerminalStreamChunkError as fatal without retrying, each occurrence halted the loop until a manual 'continue' was entered (adding 11.75m / 705.2s of idle wait time excluded from the 96m active duration).

notesDetails.title: Friction Between ZCode's Stateful File Guards and mix format (27 Python/Sed Mutations)
bullets: Read-State Invalidated by mix format: ZCode's Edit and Write tools reject modifications if a file's mtime changed since its last Read, while Read rejects re-reading an unchanged file ('Wasted call — file unchanged since your last Read', triggered 3 times at lines 62, 159, 194).

6 of 8 Edit/Write Errors from Linter/Formatter Drift: Running mix format via Bash updated file mtimes on disk and caused 6 Edit/Write calls (lines 96, 139, 170, 178, 182, 226) to fail with 'File has been modified since read, either by the user or by a linter.'

Workaround via Inline Python Patching: To avoid extra Read round-trips after formatting, the agent executed 27 file mutations via python3 - <<'EOF' or sed -i inside Bash so it could patch, run mix format, and run mix test in a single turn.

notesDetails.title: Two Subtle Bugs Caught and Fixed via Systematic Isolation (S3 & S7)
bullets:
1. The :binary.split/2 Single-Split Trap in HTTP Header Parsing (S3, Lines 111–129): Multi-header responses with Connection: close + Content-Length: 1 timed out after 2s while single-header responses passed. In lib/capy_bench/http.ex, [status_line | header_lines] = :binary.split(head, "
") (without :global) split only once, collapsing all headers into a single 'connection' header with an embedded '
content-length: 1' so no framing was recognized and the client waited for EOF. Switching to String.split(head, "
") at line 128 fixed it.

2. Interrupted In-Flight Elapsed-Time Accounting (S7, Lines 242–259): When Ctrl-C arrived at 1.2s during a stalled request that settled at its 2.0s timeout, Elapsed reported ~1.29s instead of ~2.0s. lib/capy_bench/runner.ex initially computed Elapsed from interrupted_at even when an in-flight request was still settling; adding interrupt_in_flight?: state.sched.in_flight (line 258) switched Elapsed to last_settle_at when interrupted mid-flight.
